title: A Witness for the Inheritance
premise: Tamsin Amberdale, a true-crime podcaster famous for closing every case they take, is drawn into a thirty-year-old disappearance when a fresh corpse surfaces wearing clothes lifted from Tamsin's own closet—clothes only someone who had been watching them could have taken. The victim is connected to the Amberdale inheritance and to the witness who vanished the night Tamsin's aunt died, a witness Tamsin suspects was never a stranger at all. As Tamsin peels back alibis stitched together by three families bound by an old estate, they discover the killer is the one person who claimed to be protecting them, and that the 'witness' was their own presumed-dead parent living in hiding. In the end Tasmis trades their anonymity for the truth, broadcasts the confession, and chooses the ragtag found family of listeners and collaborators who stood by them over the poisoned legacy of blood.
about_author: Ines Ravensworth is the pen name of a former estate lawyer who spent a decade untangling inheritance disputes in rural England before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about the lies families keep in attics, ledgers, and love letters.

chapters.title: The Coldest File
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In their cluttered studio, Tamsin closes their 47th case on air and vows the next will be the coldest on record: the 1994 disappearance of witness Marlowe Vane. A listener's voicemail hints Marlowe never left town. Beat: restless triumph masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Clothes That Aren't Mine
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Police call Tamsin to a canal-side crime scene: a dead man dressed in Tamsin's own missing cardigan and scarf. Detective Sergeant Idris Okafor is skeptical of podcaster involvement. Beat: violation—the watcher has become the watched.

chapters.title: The Amberdale Clause
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Digging into the victim, solicitor Edmund Pryce, Tamsin finds he handled the Amberdale estate—their own family's—and his death coincides with the thirtieth anniversary of Aunt Rosalind's fatal fall. Beat: the case was always personal.

chapters.title: Listeners and Liars
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with producer Wren, who runs the show's fan network. Wren maps tip-offs and notices one informant, 'Nightjar,' predicted the murder location a day early. Beat: unease inside the found family.

chapters.title: Thirty-Year Alibi
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Interview of elderly housekeeper Bess Carnow, whose 1994 statement placed Marlowe Vane at the estate gate at 9 p.m.—the same hour Rosalind fell. Bess recants a detail she's repeated for decades. Beat: the past shifting underfoot.

chapters.title: What the Closet Knew
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Forensics show the stolen clothes were taken over months, not stolen in one night—someone had access to Tamsin's flat. Tamsin scans old recordings and hears a floorboard creak in an empty room. Beat: paranoia blooming.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Games
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. The detective works his own angle: Pryce was blackmailing two heirs over a codicil that disinherited the Amberdale line. He warns Tamsin off, but shares the codicil's existence. Beat: grudging alliance.

chapters.title: Nightjar Sings
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren traces Nightjar's IP to a decommissioned gatehouse on the old Amberdale land and goes alone, finding a wall of clippings about Tamsin—photos, timelines, a child's drawing signed 'T.A.' Beat: dread and tenderness entangled.

chapters.title: Rosalind's Last Winter
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In the county archive, Tamsin reads Rosalind's letters hinting she was shielding someone from prosecution, and that Marlowe Vane saw 'the wrong Amberdale' die. Beat: grief reframed as cover-up.

chapters.title: A Body in the Well
chapters.summary: Tamsin's and Okafor's POV. A second death: Bess Carnow, drowned in the estate's dry well hours after Tamsin's interview. The alibi network is being dismantled, witness by witness. Beat: guilt—the podcast painted the targets.

chapters.title: Suspect: Me
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Okafor is pressured to treat Tamsin as a suspect; the stolen clothes and Tamsin's fingerprints on Pryce's files look damning. Okafor hides an exculpatory detail, crossing a line. Beat: duty bending toward loyalty.

chapters.title: The Gatehouse Tapes
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Following Wren's find, Tamsin reaches the gatehouse first—too late; it's burned. In the ash, a scorched cassette labeled with Tamsin's birth name, which they've never told anyone. Beat: identity cracked open.

chapters.title: Blood and Codicil
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The codicil names a beneficiary born the year Marlowe vanished: Tamsin themselves, on condition they 'come forward as witness.' Tamsin realizes their whole anonymous life was engineered. Beat: fury at being a plot in someone else's story.

chapters.title: Everyone Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren rallies the show's community—archivists, retired coppers, listeners—to guard Tamsin and crowdsource the 1994 timeline. The found family becomes an investigation. Beat: warmth as counterweight to danger.

chapters.title: The Wrong Amberdale
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Reconstructing the night: Rosalind wasn't the target—she swapped places with Tamsin's mother, who fled as Marlowe's killer struck. The witness saw a mother's sacrifice and was paid to forget it. Beat: shattering revelation of parentage.

chapters.title: Midnight at the Mausoleum
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, tense and claustrophobic. A summons in Rosalind's handwriting lures Tamsin to the estate crypt; someone locks the door behind them. Beat: the trap closes.

chapters.title: The Protector
chapters.summary: Climax, Tamsin's POV. The killer is revealed as Tamsin's lifelong 'uncle' and legal guardian, who killed Pryce and Bess to bury the codicil and keep Tamsin invisible—his twisted duty of protection. Tamsin, wearing a live mic Wren insisted on, records his confession. Beat: love against duty, weaponized and survived.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Okafor makes the arrest; the team debates airing the tape. They broadcast the confession unedited, and Tamsin speaks their birth name on air for the first time, claiming both selves. Beat: catharsis, exposure chosen freely.

chapters.title: What the Witness Saw
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Following the confession's thread, Tamsin finds Marlowe Vane alive—elderly, hidden, the original witness kept quiet by guilt. Marlowe's testimony completes the case and frees Tamsin's mother's name. Beat: the coldest case, closed.

chapters.title: Terms of the Estate
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin declines the Amberdale inheritance, redirecting it to a fund for witnesses and cold-case families, and signs the estate over to the community land trust. Beat: refusing poisoned legacy.

chapters.title: A Family of Listeners
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The team records a live finale; listeners fill the hall. Tamsin and Wren admit what they mean to each other—love chosen, not assigned. Beat: found family made official.

chapters.title: The Next Cold File
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, epilogue. A new voicemail arrives: another witness, another decade of silence. Tamsin smiles, hits record, and promises to close this one too—no longer hiding, never again alone. Beat: forward motion, scars carried lightly.
